text.p: These are the leading stories in Botswana's independent weekly newspapers The Guardian and Mmegi (The Reporter) on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The opposition Botswana National Front has slammed a new proposed Mass Media Communications Bill, saying it is ironic that as other members of the Southern African Development Community embrace openness and transparency, "Botswana choses to move backwards".
- A pair of Siamese twins died after an operation to separate them.
- Five convicted murderers will appeal their death sentences beore the Court of Appeal on July 7. The court will hear 13 other appeals of lesser ciminal matters and 13 civil cases.

- A delegation from the Namibia-based Media Institute of Southern Africa (MISA) met the minister responsible for broadcasting and information, Ponatshego Kedikilwe, in an effort to win a delay of the proposed new law on mass media. The minister will meet MISA officials for further talks next week.
- The most compelling argument for Botswana to resume limited trade in ivory was that it would use funds generated for the benefit of rural communities.
